html:
Peter Claver was a Spanish Jesuit priest who spent nearly forty years caring for enslaved Africans arriving at Cartagena, in today's Colombia. He was made a saint in 1888.

Born in Catalonia, he came to Cartagena in 1610, when it was a chief port of the Atlantic slave trade. When ships arrived he went into the holds with food, water and medicine, nursed the sick and baptised many thousands, through interpreters. He called himself the slave of the slaves forever.

He did not oppose slavery itself, as few did then, but he insisted that Africans were full human beings. He died in Cartagena in 1654. The Catholic Church made him patron of slaves and of African missions, and Colombia marks its day of human rights on his feast.
